summary: Escoheag Hill tower, Kent County RI: first built 1934 in Burrillville, moved 1937, rebuilt 1938; cab burned after 2009; registers disagree on what stands.

facts.status_note: Registers disagree. One describes abandoned remains; the 2017 NHLR entry describes a standing tower whose cab was burned after 2009.
facts.agency: Rhode Island Department of Environmental Management

events.note: NHLR: first built on an unnamed knoll in George Washington State Forest, Burrillville (the earlier site)
NHLR says moved in 1937 to Escoheag Hill; Forest Lookouts quotes a 1937 plan to move it
NHLR says reconstructed at its present location; FFLOS says built by the CCC in 1938
Not an active lookout since around 1990 (NHLR, approximate)
NHLR registration June 9, 2017; nominated by Jack Kelley

corrections.why: NHLR (2017) and the Forest Fire Lookout Association list describe a standing structure with its cab gone; the FFLOS page says only abandoned remains. Human check needed: if the two registrations are the same structure, the gone status is contested.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: FFLOS credits the CCC with building an 80-foot tower here in 1938. NHLR says a tower was first built in 1934 in Burrillville, moved in 1937 and reconstructed here in 1938. The Forest Lookouts George Washington page supports the 1934 build and the planned 1937 move. Both agree on 1938 at this site.

FFLOS lists abandoned remains; NHLR (2017) and the Forest Fire Lookout Association list a standing structure without its cab. The two registrations give different coordinates, so it is not clear they describe one structure. Not resolved.

notes_for_editor: Status is contested. FFLOS: abandoned remains. NHLR 2017: standing, cab burned after 2009, not maintained. FLA list: Standing* (cab gone). Unknown whether these describe one structure; the coordinates differ. Staffing end around 1990 is approximate per NHLR. The 1934 George Washington tower is the same chain as the Escoheag Hill tower per NHLR and Forest Lookouts, but the George Washington FFLOS record is a separate site. No source on public access; the story advises against climbing. NHLR 2017 photo credited to Jack Kelley is not added (licence unknown).
